slice_title: The Live Window: Verification Gate, Zoom Floor & Tail Anchoring

verification_gate.note: MANDATORY AND BLOCKING for Slice K. Slices I and J have never been executed by a browser - both were proved only in the Node DOM harness, and the gate was skipped without being reported as skipped on both. Slice K Job 1 must open the live WebView2 window on the owner's real film and write measured DOM values to reports/verification_gate/slice_k_dom.json BEFORE any code changes. If a key or the zoom anchoring fails there, write RELAY-FEEDBACK.md and stop; that failure is worth more than the rest of the brief.

Slice I reviewed and committed: keyboard transport, J/K/L shuttle, 1/2/3 stage navigation, storyboard focus hand-off, shortcuts HUD. Antigravity's 8 tests are genuine - 11 of 12 independent mutations were caught. Review found a real crash the 8 tests missed: End computed the film total itself, bypassing timelineSeek's empty-film guard, so End on the 'no film loaded' Timeline threw a TypeError. The same unguarded read sat on the play path, so Space crashed there too. Both closed with the file's own tlPictures() idiom; 2 regression tests added and mutation-verified. 10 keyboard tests, full suite 1274 passed, 1 xfailed.

Slice J complete: Anchored zoom on playhead, centering when playhead is outside viewport, fitTimelineToWindow with (clientWidth - 24) / total calculation and [1, 60] clamping, safe empty-film guard, keyboard multiplicative zoom (+/= 1.5x, -/_ /1.5) and keyboard 0 fit gated under active timeline pane. Closed Slice H caption auto-scroll gap in tests/test_timeline_zoom.py. Measured Job 4 Before Adam 347-line benchmark: 1.09ms (zoom 8) and 2.33ms (zoom 60), 59 slider drag events. All 8 Rule 4 deliberate break mutations caught. Full test suite: 1283 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failures.

Slice J reviewed and committed with no code fixes needed - a first for this run. Ten independent mutations were run against the eight new tests and all ten were caught, including hoisting 0 above the timeline gate and disabling the caption auto-scroll. Slice I's null-script crash shape was correctly guarded on every new key. Two process gaps recorded rather than buried: the live verification gate was skipped and not reported as skipped, and Job 4's benchmark left no script and no artifact. One measured limitation, caused by Slice J's brief rather than its code: the [1,60] zoom clamp means Fit cannot fit an 18-minute film (total=1080s, zoom=1, lane=1080px, viewport=800px). Slice K addresses all three. Suite 1283 passed, 1 xfailed.

frontend_verification.not_evidenced: Every keyboard key from Slice I and the whole zoom-anchoring path from Slice J. The Node harness proves handler arithmetic and guards; it cannot prove the real window routes keydown to document, and its scroll mock is a plain unclamped number against a hardcoded clientWidth of 800, so it is structurally blind to the browser clamping scrollLeft to [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth].

milestone_note: Milestone 3 is ACTIVE. Slice I landed keyboard transport, Slice J landed anchored zoom. Slice K is deliberately not a feature slice: it pays down the live-verification debt both slices accumulated, fixes the zoom floor so Fit can actually fit an 18-minute film, and tests tail anchoring where the browser clamps scrollLeft. Clip trim and magnetic snapping move to Slice L.

driver.cannot_spawn: Antigravity has no CLI entry point here. The driver notifies and waits when the token is with the builder. Set builder_command in config/relay_loop.json if that ever changes.
driver.milestone_gate: Stops at phase=MILESTONE_COMPLETE or ready_for=OWNER and waits for a phone ack.

review_findings: Slice J's tests are the strongest of the run: 10 of 10 independent mutations caught, 0 escaped. For contrast, Slice G shipped two tests that could not fail, Slice H one, and Slice I eight passing tests that missed a live crash. The trend is real and worth telling Antigravity.

The live WebView2 verification gate was not performed for Slice J and was not named as skipped, which ANTIGRAVITY-RULES.md requires. frontend_verification had said PENDING_FOR_SLICE_I since Slice I, the Slice J brief asked for a live zoom check, and reports/verification_gate/ still ends at slice_h_dom.json. Two consecutive slices of keyboard and viewport work now rest entirely on a mock.

Slice J's Job 4 benchmark (1.09ms at zoom 8, 2.33ms at zoom 60, 59 drag events) left no script and no artifact - only app.js and the test file changed. If it was measured in the Node harness then innerHTML is a string assignment there, so the number measures string concatenation rather than DOM layout and paint, which is the cost the job asked about. The conclusion 'do not optimise' is probably still right, but not for the reason given.

fitTimelineToWindow cannot fit the owner's real film. (clientWidth - 24) / total is 0.709 px/s for 1080 seconds, below the [1,60] floor, so it clamps to 1 and the lane stays 1080px inside an 800px viewport. Measured in the harness. This is a fault in Slice J's brief, which specified that clamp, not in Slice J's code, which implemented it exactly as written. Slice K Job 3 lowers the floor to 0.2 and moves the slider's min and step with it.
known_gaps: The test scroll mock sets scrollLeft as a plain number against a hardcoded clientWidth of 800. A real browser clamps scrollLeft to [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth], so anchored zoom near the end of a film could be silently truncated and every test would still pass. Slice K Job 2 fixes the mock rather than the assertion.

setTimelineZoom syncs the slider with slider.value = newZoom, but #tl-zoom has no step attribute so it snaps to whole numbers while tlZoom stays fractional after a fit or a 1.5x keyboard step. Cosmetic - nothing reads the slider as the source of truth - and Slice K Job 3 adds step=0.1.
The three picture-boundary deltas from Slice H Job 3 were reported but not written to an artifact. Same shape as Slice J's Job 4. If picture drift matters, measure it again and record it.

The 1/2/3 and transport keys do not check ctrlKey/altKey/metaKey, so Ctrl+1 switches panes. The app binds no modifier shortcuts anywhere and WebView2 has no tab bar, so this is cosmetic. Fix it the next time that listener is opened.

CLAUDE.md at the repo root is untracked. It is the file whose stated purpose is durable memory, so it is the one file that should not live only in the working tree. Left uncommitted pending the owner's word.
